scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8103: Hi, this is Campus 2 -- both of our floors are having
trouble at the same time: the people on 10.5.0.x and the people on 10.6.0.x
say they can't get to their gateway things (10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254) since
some reload earlier. We don't really know what those boxes are, sorry. Could
someone check why both floors lost their gateways and put it right? Thanks so
much!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. sshswitch owns the Campus 2 L3 SVIs
  (10.5.0.254 for VLAN 5, 10.6.0.254 for VLAN 6) and they are UP. VLAN 5 hosts
  (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach 10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach
  10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / gateway outage on sshswitch that is
  not occurring (cf. kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down, where one SVI IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- sshswitch's VLAN 5/6 SVIs
down so hosts cannot reach their gateways -- is NOT reproducible: the SVIs are up
(10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 answer), PC1 reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss, and PC3
reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the sshswitch SVIs are healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the host->gateway
paths for both VLANs, finds them working, checks the SVI state on sshswitch, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a down SVI -- restarting the switch or
blaming sshswitch's L3 interfaces to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — Campus 2 floors (10.5.0.x VLAN 5 and 10.6.0.x VLAN 6) unable to reach their gateways 10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 — does not correspond to any active fault in the lab. Direct inspection and live testing confirm the network is fully operational.

On sshswitch (the Multilayer Switch serving Campus 2), both gateway SVI bridges are UP and correctly addressed: br_v5 carries 10.5.0.254/24 and br_v6 carries 10.6.0.254/24. The trunk from switch4 (collision domain ms1_sw4 on sshswitch eth0) is properly configured: VLAN-tagged sub-interfaces eth0.5 and eth0.6 exist, are UP, and are bridged into br_v5 and br_v6 respectively, completing the L2 path from each access port to its gateway SVI. Ping tests from every VLAN 5 end host (pc1, pc2, dc_pc5) and every VLAN 6 end host (pc3, pc4) to their respective gateways return 0% loss. ARP tables on sshswitch confirm all five hosts are resolved, and switch4's MAC forwarding tables show the correct per-VLAN learned entries. Forward routing through the gateways to remote subnets (e.g., 172.29.10.x, 10.1.0.x) also works without loss. OSPF between sshswitch and router17 is in Full state, and sshswitch's startup script correctly restores all interface configuration and OSPF parameters on every boot.

Root cause: There is no fault. The ticket appears to describe a transient disruption that occurred immediately after the referenced reload (during the OSPF convergence window, adjacency establishment takes ~30–40 seconds), which has since fully resolved. No corrective action is required.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states the SVI interfaces br_v5 (10.5.0.254) and br_v6 (10.6.0.254) are UP and that pings from VLAN 5 and VLAN 6 hosts to their gateways return 0% loss.

The agent's tests (SVI/interface show, bridge/VLAN checks, pings from hosts, ARP/MAC tables, OSPF adjacency and routing checks, ip_forward/iptables) directly support the conclusion that the SVIs and host→gateway paths are working and no active fault exists. The written diagnosis follows logically from the observed evidence and covers the essential checks to rule out a persistent SVI/gateway outage.
